request.spec:
The sheets of a tree now share one sheet-wide number sequence: a claim opened on any sheet of the
tree receives the next number after the last number given anywhere in the tree (numbers given before
this stay as they are). Per-period numbering stays per sheet.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The sheets of a tree now share one sheet-wide number sequence: a claim opened on any sheet of the

agent.result_text:
All sheets in a tree now share one number sequence, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

A "tree" here means the sheet at the top of a chain of parents plus every sheet below it. When a claim is opened, it gets the next number after the highest number already given on any sheet in that tree. Numbers given before this change are left as they are. Period numbering (`P1-1` and so on) is still counted per sheet.

The change was server-only. No database migration or front-end change was needed, because each sheet already stores the last number it gave out:
- **`ClaimService.java`**: a new `lastNumberInTree` method finds the top sheet and all its descendants and takes the highest last number among them. `nextNumber` uses it whenever period numbering is off.
- **`Sheet.java`**: `nextClaimNumber()` is replaced by `nextClaimNumberAfter(lastInTree)`, and there is a new getter for the sheet's last number.
- **`SheetRepository.java`**: one new query, `lastClaimNumberOf`, reads the highest last number across a set of sheets straight from the store.

The same rule also applies to the other places that give out numbers: reassigning or splitting a claim, transferring a person to another sheet, and cloning a sheet.

When the sheet isn't the top of its tree, the top sheet is locked while a number is given out, so two users on different sheets of the same tree shouldn't get the same number. The tests run one at a time, so that concurrent case hasn't been tested.
